questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to go to Iceland, but the subject of the course was also interesting. Because the course had a post-colonial perspective when it comes to Denmark and Iceland, I really wanted to go because it was something I didn't really know about. I think it's healthy to acknowledge the history of your country, also the parts you perhaps are not proud of.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: a littel overwhelming at the beginning, but quiet easy when you gor into it

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We could always write an email if we needed help with the process. They replied quickly.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was almost the same; we worked more in groups, which was a good thing because it was an exchange course.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
People are polite, and you can always ask for help. 
Take some extra pocket money with you; Iceland is quite expensive.
The education is good, all in all you wont regret it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Get to know other students from other contries that studie the same as you. 
Meeting the host country's leading researchers in their fields.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Because of the post-colonial perspective, there were some topics that were sensitive, understandably. But it made some discussions quite difficult to have, because you had to balance between the academic perspective and, at the same time, show respect for the sensitivity. But I think it was a great and healthy challenge.
